newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX gasoline ends sharply up on French strike.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX gasoline ends sharply up on French strike.

text.p: NYMEX gasoline ended with steep gains Tuesday as a major refinery strike in France threatened to decrease U.S. imports and tighten supply.
The gasoline rally reflects keen buying interest by local players which have fueled gains in gasoline since last week, dealers said.
"They were looking for an excuse to buy. There was buying in the spreads even before the strike," said Rocky D'Esposito, trader with RJ Futures.
January gasoline settled up 1.01 cents a gallon at 69.13 cents after rising to a contract high of 69.70 cents.

Workers of French oil giant Elf Aquitaine entered their sixth day of a strike at three refineries with a total capacity of 440,000 barrels a day. The strike has crippled a third of French capacity and three quarters of Elf's European refining network.

Gasoline's gains boosted crude and heating oil prices with January crude ending 13 cents up at $24.93 a barrel and January heating oil finishing 0.65 cent a gallon higher at 74.22 cents. Stocks of gasoline were forecasted by traders to show a minor build in weekly oil inventory data by the American Petroleum Institute (API) expected Tuesday evening.
But, some traders said there could be a bullish draw in gasoline stocks due to strong demand, evidenced by active refiner buying in the cash market.
When the API data was released following the market's close, it actually showed a bearish build in gasoline stocks of 1.93 million barrels. The data reflects the week ended November 29.
"If there is any sign of weakness, you are going to see it in the Jan/Feb gasoline spread which has blown out sharply in such a short period," said R.J. Futures' D'Esposito.
The Jan/Feb gasoline spread has widened to 1.70 cents from 0.86 cent at Monday's open.
Countering the bearish stock build for gasoline is a statement by the union representing the Elf Aquitaine workers that the strike was extended to at least Wednesday morning.
The API data showed a larger-than-expected build in distillate stocks of 1.85 million barrels and a minor 868,000 barrel draw in crude stocks.
This is the fourth consecutive week the API data has shown a draw in crude stocks.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
